name: Founder decision: Rule who holds a lead's check-in
text_content:
P21 and finding 19.7. The record has feedback running both directions and every new person on a ninety-day plan with regular check-ins, and the two leads are parallel with no one above them; no one is named to hold a lead's six check-ins. The team recommends a partner under Session 3's Class C rule: the Maitre d's with Brandon's seat, the Operations Lead's with the partner whose domain holds the outcome, and both partners once at the sixth where the plan crosses both. The interval is the ledger's, every two weeks. Blocks the first lead's second check-in and readiness row 88. High.

Filed by Session 7 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmhrz. Reasoning lives on the S7 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

comment.text: Session 14 adds three dependencies to this ruling. A lead's own horizon window has no holder and no trigger until it closes; the team's reading, held for Session 15, is that it opens by the stack on the leads' review record's counts (node overload on the seat across the thresholds, "something new" reviews per period, the domain's upward halves read by mechanism) and never on a person's line about the lead, and is held by whoever holds the lead's check-in against the lead seat's own sheet. A non-negotiable flag whose subject is a lead has its flag read held by the other lead with a founder, and the decision is the founders'. And the performance page's line on a lead's window reads "held" until this ruling lands. The team repeats the recommendation to close it before the leads are in the building. S14 page, sections 6.6 and 10.3; P28, P36.

comment.text: Session 13 adds the review's dependency: a lead's review has no holder until this closes, and the team's reading is that the holder is whoever holds the lead's check-in, on the same form, against the lead's own sheet, with dimension one as holding a domain without an apex, dimension two from the lead's own advocate record, dimension three as the lead's range on the leads' review record, and dimension four as what the building supplied to the lead's seat including its languages. The review's upward half makes the undestined concern sharper, because a review is the one formal moment the record promises for feedback about management and a person's read of their lead goes, at present, only to their lead; the team's reading that a lead's review holder reads the domain's upward halves aggregated by mechanism is held for Session 15. Until the ruling the founders hold the first leads' reviews by default as they hold their check-ins. S13 page, sections 6.5 and 8.5; P16, P20.

comment.text: Session 12 adds the coaching model's reasons for urgency. Every coaching act on the floor is the Maitre d's, and every trigger in the S12 decision-rights entries that reads "for the Maitre d's own" has no destination until this closes: a hypothesis or summary the Maitre d writes anywhere, a trait word or "disengaged" the Maitre d says at a check-in, a correction delivered between check-ins outside a placed one, a placed check-in with a reason found anywhere, a recognition decline said at the brief, and a re-training trigger on the Maitre d's own scorecard, which is today a load line at the partners' review that no one reads with the Maitre d. Blame absorption stops one seat short: management absorbs blame from staff and the customer, and nothing absorbs it from a lead (S12 finding 18.5). Until this closes, the only people who could hold a lead's check-in are the founders, which is why the coaching module is completed by the founders pre-opening. S12 page, sections 7.3, 12, 15.9, and 18.5; P43.
